title: Adopt a Tree: Parent Guide
endLine: Winter buds hold next spring's leaves while the tree rests.

scenes.tts: In winter, a bare tree looks dead. It's easy to walk past the same tree and miss its slow changes. Yet one tree, visited through the year, tells a very different story.
scenes.caption: In winter, a bare tree looks dead. It's easy to walk past the same tree and miss its slow changes. Yet one tree, visited through the year, tells a very different story.
scenes.visual: Warm schematic illustration on a soft pale-blue winter sky. A single large broadleaf tree fills 65 percent of the frame height on the right, branches bare and swaying gently in a slow breeze. A wooden fence post stands on the left lawn. Above the bare crown, large high-contrast text fades in: 'Bare in winter. Dead?' No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: In winter, a bare tree looks dead. It's easy to walk past the same tree and miss its slow changes. Yet one tree, visited through the year, tells a very different story.

scenes.visual: Same tree and fence post stay anchored in place. Soft light sweeps across the sky as the title 'Adopt a Tree' appears cleanly on the left above the fence post, with a subtle season ring turning slowly around the tree crown.

scenes.tts: Adopting one tree slows the year down. Your child practices looking closely and recording slow changes over time. They make a guess, wait, and check it against real evidence. In thirty minutes to start, you set up a whole year.
scenes.caption: Adopting one tree slows the year down. Your child practices looking closely and recording slow changes over time. They make a guess, wait, and check it against real evidence. In thirty minutes to start, you set up a whole year.
scenes.visual: Same world, now shifting to early fall with green-and-gold leaves gently rustling. Next to the fence post, a simple schematic folder opens cleanly to show a crayon twig sketch and a tiny calendar row. Three short labels appear one by one beside the folder: 'Look closely', 'Predict and check', '30 minutes to start'. Gentle drifting leaf motion continues.
scenes.narration: Adopting one tree slows the year down. Your child practices looking closely and recording slow changes over time. They make a guess, wait, and check it against real evidence. In thirty minutes to start, you set up a whole year.

scenes.tts: Choose a tree that drops its leaves in fall. Ask permission to visit. Bring a phone or camera, paper, and a pencil. Stand ten to twenty steps back by a landmark. Take every photo from that same spot, facing the same way. Keep the whole tree in the frame.
scenes.caption: Choose a tree that drops its leaves in fall. Ask permission to visit. Bring a phone or camera, paper, and a pencil. Stand ten to twenty steps back by a landmark. Take every photo from that same spot, facing the same way. Keep the whole tree in the frame.
scenes.visual: Same broadleaf tree on the right; a small evergreen pine fades out in the background with a gentle X so the broadleaf tree stays the focus. Footstep dots animate across the lawn from the tree to the wooden fence post on the left with a clean bracket labeled '10 to 20 steps'. An illustrated hand holds up a simple schematic phone frame aligned with the tree, locking a dotted viewfinder rectangle around the whole crown.
scenes.narration: Choose a tree that drops its leaves in fall. Ask permission to visit. Bring a phone or camera, paper, and a pencil. Stand ten to twenty steps back by a landmark. Take every photo from that same spot, facing the same way. Keep the whole tree in the frame.

scenes.tts: Before looking closely, let your child predict first. Ask, 'What do you think this tree will look like next month?' Save the guess. Spend about ten minutes looking at bark, a low twig, the weather, and any animals nearby. Your child draws one twig or leaf to save in a folder.
scenes.caption: Before looking closely, let your child predict first. Ask, 'What do you think this tree will look like next month?' Save the guess. Spend about ten minutes looking at bark, a low twig, the weather, and any animals nearby. Your child draws one twig or leaf to save in a folder.
scenes.visual: Camera smoothly zooms closer to the same tree's trunk and a low branch while keeping the sky visible. A clean speech bubble pops above the left side: 'What will it look like next month?' Then a schematic notebook page appears in the corner as simple drawn icons settle gently near the trunk: rough bark lines, a small sun-and-cloud symbol, a perched bird silhouette, and a pencil sketching one low twig.
scenes.narration: Before looking closely, let your child predict first. Ask, 'What do you think this tree will look like next month?' Save the guess. Spend about ten minutes looking at bark, a low twig, the weather, and any animals nearby. Your child draws one twig or leaf to save in a folder.

scenes.tts: Come back about once a month for fifteen minutes, or once each season. Repeat the photo and drawing. Record what you saw. Check the last guess, then compare photos. Ask, 'Can you find three differences?'
scenes.caption: Come back about once a month for fifteen minutes, or once each season. Repeat the photo and drawing. Record what you saw. Check the last guess, then compare photos. Ask, 'Can you find three differences?'
scenes.visual: Pull back to the same fence-post view. Two crisp schematic photo frames of the same tree slide side by side in the center-left—green summer crown beside yellowing fall crown with leaves drifting down. Three bright highlight rings pulse softly over differences (leaf color, fewer leaves on the branches, fallen leaves) as a speech bubble reads: 'Find three differences?' Label below: '15 min monthly (or 4x/year)'.
scenes.narration: Come back about once a month for fifteen minutes, or once each season. Repeat the photo and drawing. Record what you saw. Check the last guess, then compare photos. Ask, 'Can you find three differences?'

scenes.tts: Now picture your winter visit. The branches are bare, and your child says, 'Our tree died.' Before you explain, pause for a moment. What do you predict you'll see if you look closely at a bare winter twig?
scenes.caption: Now picture your winter visit. The branches are bare, and your child says, 'Our tree died.' Before you explain, pause for a moment. What do you predict you'll see if you look closely at a bare winter twig?
scenes.visual: The same tree transitions to crisp winter bareness under a cool gray-blue sky, branches swaying softly. A large circular zoom inset opens smoothly over a single bare twig on the right, filling 60 percent of the frame height. High-contrast question card sits clearly on the left: 'What will you see on a bare winter twig?'
scenes.narration: Now picture your winter visit. The branches are bare, and your child says, 'Our tree died.' Before you explain, pause for a moment. What do you predict you'll see if you look closely at a bare winter twig?

scenes.visual: Hold the exact winter twig zoom and question card on screen for thinking time. Keep subtle ambient motion: the bare twig sways slightly and a slow, soft progress ring moves quietly beneath the question without revealing the answer.

scenes.tts: Look closely at a bare twig. Plump buds wait at the tip and where each leaf joined. Ask, 'I wonder what is inside this bud. What do you think will come out?' The tree is dormant, alive but resting, with next spring's leaves folded inside.
scenes.caption: Look closely at a bare twig. Plump buds wait at the tip and where each leaf joined. Ask, 'I wonder what is inside this bud. What do you think will come out?' The tree is dormant, alive but resting, with next spring's leaves folded inside.
scenes.visual: In the same twig zoom, warm golden circles highlight a plump bud at the twig tip and a smaller side bud where a leaf stalk met the twig. A clean cutaway schematic shows tiny green folded leaves tucked neatly inside the bud scales. Short high-contrast labels appear: 'Dormant = alive, resting' and 'Buds hold spring leaves'. A speech bubble briefly echoes: 'What is inside this bud?'
scenes.narration: Look closely at a bare twig. Plump buds wait at the tip and where each leaf joined. Ask, 'I wonder what is inside this bud. What do you think will come out?' The tree is dormant, alive but resting, with next spring's leaves folded inside.

scenes.tts: Shorter days and cooler weather in fall signal the tree to drop its leaves before winter. Warmer spring days wake those buds. When you finish all four seasons, put one picture from each season in order. Look at the order together and ask what comes next.
scenes.caption: Shorter days and cooler weather in fall signal the tree to drop its leaves before winter. Warmer spring days wake those buds. When you finish all four seasons, put one picture from each season in order. Look at the order together and ask what comes next.
scenes.visual: Zoom back out to the carried tree-and-fence-post scene. A clean schematic sun arc lowers in the sky while a simple thermometer bar dips, triggering leaves to drift down in fall; then the sun arc rises and warmth swells the buds into bright spring leaves. The view glides into a neat four-panel strip of the same tree in order: Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter, connected by a gentle curving cycle arrow.
scenes.narration: Shorter days and cooler weather in fall signal the tree to drop its leaves before winter. Warmer spring days wake those buds. When you finish all four seasons, put one picture from each season in order. Look at the order together and ask what comes next.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child on every visit. Avoid busy road crossings, storms, and strong wind. Feet stay on the ground, with no climbing. Nothing goes in a mouth, and small acorns, nuts, or stones can choke children under four. Call nine one one if choking.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child on every visit. Avoid busy road crossings, storms, and strong wind. Feet stay on the ground, with no climbing. Nothing goes in a mouth, and small acorns, nuts, or stones can choke children under four. Call nine one one if choking.
scenes.visual: Return to the friendly schematic tree on its safe lawn. Clear, high-contrast safety badges appear neatly beside the tree (at most four at once): a calm adult-and-child silhouette standing together on the grass ('Feet on ground'), a crossed-out storm cloud and road edge, and a crossed-out acorn/berry/stone icon labeled 'Under 4: choking risk — Call 911'. Gentle grass sway keeps the scene alive.
scenes.narration: Stay with your child on every visit. Avoid busy road crossings, storms, and strong wind. Feet stay on the ground, with no climbing. Nothing goes in a mouth, and small acorns, nuts, or stones can choke children under four. Call nine one one if choking.

scenes.tts: Check the trunk for poison ivy. Leave fallen nuts alone, especially with a nut allergy. Never taste wild plants, berries, or mushrooms. Look at insects without touching them. Adults handle glass lenses. Keep lenses from focusing sunlight. Never look at the sun through one. Wash hands and check for ticks.
scenes.caption: Check the trunk for poison ivy. Leave fallen nuts alone, especially with a nut allergy. Never taste wild plants, berries, or mushrooms. Look at insects without touching them. Adults handle glass lenses. Keep lenses from focusing sunlight. Never look at the sun through one. Wash hands and check for ticks.
scenes.visual: Smoothly swap the side badges on the same tree view to four clear schematic icons: a three-leaf vine on the trunk ('Leaves of three, let it be'), a stylized fuzzy caterpillar inside an eye-only look icon ('Look, don't touch'), a hand lens angled away from a bright sun, and clean soapy hands with a simple check mark ('Wash hands, tick check').
scenes.narration: Check the trunk for poison ivy. Leave fallen nuts alone, especially with a nut allergy. Never taste wild plants, berries, or mushrooms. Look at insects without touching them. Adults handle glass lenses. Keep lenses from focusing sunlight. Never look at the sun through one. Wash hands and check for ticks.

scenes.tts: By year's end, one ordinary tree becomes your child's calendar. Next winter, look for buds together when the branches turn bare again. Those tiny buds mean spring is already waiting.
scenes.caption: By year's end, one ordinary tree becomes your child's calendar. Next winter, look for buds together when the branches turn bare again. Those tiny buds mean spring is already waiting.
scenes.visual: The same tree beside its wooden fence post smoothly cycles once more from rich fall color to bare winter branches, as warm golden light softly glows on the plump twig buds. The schematic four-season folder closes neatly at the lower left while subtle light motes drift across the quiet winter sky.
scenes.narration: By year's end, one ordinary tree becomes your child's calendar. Next winter, look for buds together when the branches turn bare again. Those tiny buds mean spring is already waiting.

scenes.line: Winter buds hold next spring's leaves while the tree rests.
scenes.visual: Clean, warm end card keeping the subtle silhouette of the bare twig with plump glowing buds in the background. Centered, large, high-contrast text: 'Winter buds hold next spring's leaves while the tree rests.'
